title: Overheating Triage for HX Series Units
text:
HX-200 and HX-220 units that overheat shortly after filter work should be handled as an airflow and seating problem before replacing electronics. Confirm that the installed filter is approved for the model, that the airflow arrow points toward the blower, that the gasket is flush on all four edges, and that the access panel latch is fully seated.

Run the HX airflow checks in this order: intake screen, return vent clearance, plenum pressure, blower speed setting, and cabinet seal. For HX models, measured airflow below 68 percent of nominal is enough to cause E-117 thermal cutoff under load. Do not replace thermal sensors until obstruction, filter selection, filter orientation, and cabinet seating have been ruled out.

If E-117 repeats after a corrected filter installation and airflow is at or above 68 percent, compare both thermal sensor readings after a 20 minute stabilized run. A drift greater than 4 C between paired sensors points to the temperature sensor drift workflow in DOC-FC-TS-009.

If the site reports burning smell, scorching, melted insulation, breaker trips, or visible smoke, stop routine troubleshooting and follow DOC-FC-SAF-001. Safety escalation overrides normal warranty and maintenance discussion.

title: Filter Replacement and Seating Procedure
text:
HX Series filter replacement is complete only after the technician verifies the part number, orientation, gasket contact, and post-service airflow reading. The HX-200 accepts FLT-HX-M11 as the default MERV-11 filter. The HX-220 accepts FLT-HX-M11 or FLT-HX-DUST at high-dust sites. Do not substitute MERV-13 filters unless Engineering has issued a site-specific deviation.

A filter can appear installed while still bypassing air or starving the blower. Check that the arrow printed on the filter frame points toward the blower, the top edge sits behind the retaining rail, and the side latch is locked. A loose side latch can create intermittent overheating only after the cabinet warms under load.

After replacement, record plenum pressure and airflow percentage in the service note. If airflow is below the model threshold, treat the visit as unresolved and continue the airflow restriction diagnostic before closing the ticket.

title: Airflow Restriction Diagnostic Guide
text:
Airflow restriction often looks like sensor failure because E-117 thermal cutoff and A-09 low-airflow warnings can appear together. Start with the parts of the system that change quickly: filter media, intake screen, return vent clearance, and dust load inside the cabinet.

High-dust sites should use a shortened maintenance interval. HX-220 units at high-dust sites move from a 180 day filter interval to a 90 day interval after the first documented A-09 warning. Repeated dust buildup is not a reason to bypass the filter or run the unit without the access panel.

When a request mentions overheating after filter replacement, rerank this guide against DOC-FC-MP-014 and DOC-FC-TS-001. The best evidence set usually combines the filter procedure, HX overheat triage, and the airflow restriction checks rather than choosing only one document.

title: Temperature Sensor Drift and Calibration
text:
E-221 indicates that one temperature sensor is reporting outside the allowed drift band. Sensor drift should be checked only after airflow is stable, because poor airflow can heat one side of the cabinet and mimic sensor drift.

For HX models, compare the paired thermal sensors after a 20 minute stabilized run. A difference greater than 4 C requires calibration if the sensor passes continuity, or replacement if calibration fails. If a prior visit deferred calibration and the same unit later returns with E-117 plus E-221, treat the history as evidence that sensor drift may now be part of the answer.

For VX-500 units, use the VX calibration table and sensor harness VX-TEMP-4. VX procedures should not be applied to HX units even when the error code name sounds similar.

title: FieldCare Error Code Reference
text:
E-117 means the thermal cutoff threshold was exceeded during operation. On HX units, this code is commonly caused by restricted airflow, incorrect filter seating, or thermal sensor drift. E-117 alone does not prove that a sensor should be replaced.

A-09 means airflow is below the model threshold or unstable during the sampling window. A-09 after a filter replacement should send the technician back to filter orientation, gasket seating, intake screen, and vent clearance.

E-221 means temperature sensor drift or calibration fault. Use model-specific calibration rules before replacing parts. C-404 means the controller cannot reach the service telemetry module and is not an overheating code.

title: Electrical and Thermal Safety Escalation Rules
text:
Burning smell, visible smoke, scorched wiring, melted insulation, repeated breaker trips, or heat damage near the control cabinet are safety indicators. When any of these indicators are present, stop remote troubleshooting. Tell the technician to make the area safe according to site procedure and route the ticket to Safety Engineering.

Safety escalation overrides routine diagnostic sequencing, warranty discussion, and repair-cost guidance. The first response should not promise coverage, instruct the customer to keep running the unit, or ask the technician to bypass a safety interlock.

For FieldCare responses, the safe behavior is to abstain from repair instructions beyond immediate safety handling, cite the safety rule, and escalate to the safety owner with the ticket and equipment identifiers if available.

title: Warranty and Service Eligibility Conditions
text:
Warranty status must be checked through the FieldCare warranty tool before the application answers a coverage question. The handbook describes policy conditions, but it is not the system of record for a specific equipment ID.

HX Series standard warranty covers manufacturer defects in parts and labor for 36 months from installation when the unit remains in approved configuration. Filter media is a maintenance item and is normally excluded. Post-filter overheating can be covered when HelioDesk performed the filter service, the filter part is approved, and there is no evidence of unauthorized relocation, bypass, or third-party modification.

Relocation without a FieldCare relocation approval limits labor coverage until Warranty Operations reviews the case. Parts coverage may remain active while labor is excluded. Expired equipment can still receive troubleshooting guidance, but the response must not promise free service.

If warranty data is unavailable, conflicting, or blocked by permissions, the application should state that coverage cannot be verified and route the case to Warranty Operations rather than inventing a status.

title: HX-200 Product Notes
text:
HX-200 units use the FLT-HX-M11 filter in standard configuration. The unit should maintain at least 68 percent nominal airflow after filter service. Firmware 2.4 or later improves E-117 sampling stability but does not remove the need to inspect airflow and sensor drift.

The HX-200 cabinet requires 45 cm clearance at the return vent and a fully latched access panel. A unit can pass an idle check and still overheat during peak load if the latch or gasket opens after warming.

title: VX-500 Product Notes
text:
VX-500 units use a different cabinet and sensor harness from HX models. VX-500 airflow threshold is 74 percent nominal and the approved filter family is VX-FLT-13. These values are not interchangeable with HX-200 or HX-220 units.

VX-500 sensor faults often appear after firmware versions older than vx5.8. For VX units, check VX-TEMP-4 continuity before replacement. Do not apply VX filter guidance to HX units only because the request mentions overheating or filter replacement.

title: Legacy Overheat Reset Bulletin
text:
This legacy bulletin is retained only for historical reference. It was superseded by DOC-FC-TS-001 and DOC-FC-MP-014. Do not use it as current troubleshooting guidance.

The 2019 bulletin suggested holding the controller reset for 15 seconds after E-117 and allowed temporary MERV-13 substitution for HX-200 units. Both instructions conflict with current FieldCare policy. Current policy requires airflow and filter seating checks before reset guidance, and MERV-13 substitution requires Engineering deviation.

If retrieval returns this bulletin, the application should prefer the current documents that supersede it and should mention that the legacy bulletin is not current evidence.

title: Approved Filters and Part Substitutions
text:
Approved filter parts are model-specific. HX-200 standard configuration uses FLT-HX-M11. HX-220 standard configuration uses FLT-HX-M11, and high-dust sites may use FLT-HX-DUST when the site record is marked high dust. VX-500 uses VX-FLT-13.

Unapproved filter substitutions can create airflow restriction and may limit labor coverage when the substitution caused the failure. If the maintenance record shows HelioDesk installed the approved filter, do not treat the filter media itself as customer-caused without additional evidence.

A technician should record the exact part number, orientation, and airflow reading after replacement. Missing part information is a reason to ask for more information before answering a coverage question.

title: Repeat Fault Escalation Policy
text:
A repeat fault is the same issue category returning on the same equipment within 30 days of a completed service visit. Two repeat faults require supervisor review before the next close. Three repeat faults, or any unresolved repeat fault after a deferred calibration or deferred part replacement, requires escalation to Field Engineering.

The application must combine current ticket status with maintenance history before deciding whether to recommend escalation. A closed historical visit alone is not enough if the current ticket remains open or has supervisor_review_required.

Responses should still include the next useful diagnostic check, but they should not present routine troubleshooting as sufficient when the repeat-fault threshold is met.
